title: Planned file writes
responsibility: Preserves planned-file write operations and status formatting, with filesystem effects behind a generation adapter and formatting in a core value leaf.

inputs.name: writePlannedFiles.root
inputs.description: Base directory passed to `join(root, path)` for each planned target. The implementation does not independently validate traversal segments.

inputs.name: writePlannedFiles.files
inputs.description: Planned paths and text contents processed sequentially in array order. Identical existing text is skipped, and earlier writes remain if a later read or write rejects.

inputs.name: writePlannedFiles.options
inputs.description: Optional write policy with a default of `{}`. A truthy `force` allows replacing differing existing contents.

inputs.name: ensureParents.root
inputs.description: Base directory passed to `join(root, path)` when deriving each parent directory. The implementation does not independently validate traversal segments.

inputs.name: ensureParents.files
inputs.description: Planned paths used to derive destination parent directories. Distinct directory names are created recursively; the files themselves are not written.

inputs.name: renderFileList.files
inputs.description: Write results rendered in array order. The function reads each result's `status` and `path` and performs no filesystem access.

outputs.name: writePlannedFiles
outputs.description: On success, resolves to one result per input file in order, preserving `path` and `contents` with status `created`, `skipped`, or `overwritten`.

outputs.name: ensureParents
outputs.description: Completes after all distinct planned parent directories exist; returns no data.

outputs.name: renderFileList
outputs.description: Returns one line per result in input order, with two spaces followed by the status label and path; lines are joined with newline characters.

errors.name: ExpectedCliError
errors.description: Rejects with the overwrite-refusal message when an existing target has different contents and `options.force` is falsy.

errors.name: Filesystem failure
errors.description: A non-`ENOENT` read failure, write failure, or recursive `mkdir` failure is rethrown unchanged.
